_doc.units: type and stroke values are % of canvas width; points = pct/100 * width_in * 72. Margins are fractions of canvas width on all four sides.
_doc.canvas: Author at width_in x height_in with figure dpi 100 (1 in = 1 canvas px / 100). Export at export_dpi. display_px is the width the reader sees; min_text_px is checked there.
_doc.roles: title (bold, #333333), subtitle (#767676), label (ticks, axis titles, direct labels, value labels), annotation (#595959), source (source, notes, credit).
_doc.strokes: line = context/default line width, accent_line = highlighted series, marker = dot diameter, grid = gridline/spine width.
_doc.title_chars_2_lines: characters that fit across both title lines at the preset's title size and block width (canvas minus left and right margins), the minimum over sample takeaway sentences measured by evident.fits_title in Helvetica Neue (Helvetica and Arial metrics are within 2%; DejaVu Sans fits about 15% fewer). A rough guide only: fits_title(text, dest) measures a specific text exactly, and check_chart's title-too-long uses it.
_doc.subtitle_chars_2_lines: the same for the subtitle's two lines (evident.fits_subtitle).
_doc.bar_rows: horizontal-bar rows whose category labels fit at row pitch >= 1.6 label heights under a one-line title and subtitle, measured with evident.figure and titles. fixed_height: the destination cannot grow taller, so more rows means fewer rows or more panels, not a taller canvas.
_doc.plot_aspect: band for the main plot box (width / height, after the title block and labels) on any preset: widest 3.5:1 (one-line title and subtitle on the 16:9 slide leave about 3.2:1), tallest 1:2; horizontal-bar and category-row charts may run taller (their height follows the row count). evident.titles warns and check_chart's plot-aspect flags a plot outside it.

blog.desc: Inline blog/article image, desktop-first content column. Default when destination is unknown.

social.desc: 1080x1080 feed image; use for X (and any square feed). Type scale approved by Randy.

social_portrait.desc: 1080x1350 (4:5) feed image; use for LinkedIn and Instagram (most feed space). 25% more height for a two-line title and annotations.

slide.desc: 16:9 slide, 1920x1080 (13.333 x 7.5 in in PowerPoint). Title ~36 pt, labels ~20 pt, source ~15 pt on the slide.

report.desc: Full-width report/PDF figure, 6.25 in wide; save .pdf or .svg (vector). Title 13 pt, labels 9 pt, source 9 pt.

mobile.desc: Separate small-screen version shown 360 CSS px wide (4:5), exported 3x. Cut content before shrinking type.
